findings.title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates connectedCalendars, leaving stale cache status in the UI
findings.body: The `deleteCacheMutation` only calls the optional `onSuccess` prop on success. Unlike the `disconnectMutation` in the same file (which invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `viewer.apps.integrations` in `onSettled`), it does not invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. The `cacheUpdatedAt` value shown in this dropdown comes from that query, so after a successful cache deletion the dropdown continues to display 'Last updated: <old timestamp>' and keeps offering 'Delete cached data' until something else triggers a refetch. In usages where the parent does not pass `onChanged`/`onSuccess` (the prop is optional), the UI never refreshes at all. Fix: invalidate `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled`/`onSuccess` of the deleteCache mutation, mirroring the disconnect mutation.

findings.title: Handler instantiates CalendarCacheRepository directly, bypassing the calendar-cache feature flag
findings.body: The handler does `new CalendarCacheRepository()` and calls `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` unconditionally. The established pattern in this codebase is `CalendarCache.init(null)`, which returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the `calendar-cache` feature flag is disabled. Bypassing that means every `connectedCalendars` query (a hot settings-page query) now issues an extra `calendarCache.groupBy` against the database even when the feature is globally disabled, and it breaks the repository abstraction the mock exists for. Use `CalendarCache.init(null)` (or gate the enrichment on the feature flag) instead.

findings.title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds reports status for expired cache rows that will never be served
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `CalendarCache` rows by credentialId and returns `max(updatedAt)` with no `expiresAt` filter. `getCachedAvailability` only serves rows with `expiresAt >= now()` (30-day TTL), but expired rows are never deleted, so once a cache entry expires the UI will still show 'Cache Status / Last updated: <date>' and offer 'Delete cached data' for a cache that is effectively dead and will never be used. The status query should filter (or at least surface) expired entries, e.g. `where: { credentialId: { in: credentialIds }, expiresAt: { gte: new Date() } }`.

findings.title: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now writes to SelectedCalendar on the webhook hot path for a value nothing reads
findings.body: The added `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` runs on every Google webhook-driven cache refresh and updates every SelectedCalendar row for the credential (including calendars/event types whose cache was not part of this refresh) purely to bump `updatedAt`. Per the PR's own notes, `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is not displayed anywhere — the frontend reads `cacheUpdatedAt` from `CalendarCache`. This is a dead database write on a high-frequency path; it should be removed rather than merged as-is.

findings.title: Access-denied path throws a generic Error, surfacing as HTTP 500 instead of 404
findings.body: When the credential does not exist or belongs to another user, the handler does `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC converts non-`TRPCError` throws into `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (500), so a client requesting a foreign or nonexistent credentialId gets a server-error response (and a Sentry-eligible log) instead of a clean `NOT_FOUND`/`FORBIDDEN`. Throw `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND", ... })` (or FORBIDDEN) as is convention elsewhere in the codebase.

findings.title: Dev script writes GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL to the wrong env file and uses macOS-only sed syntax
findings.body: Two portability/correctness problems in this helper script: (1) `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the caller's working directory, not the script location — run from the repo root it points outside the repository, and run from `scripts/` it points at the repo-root `.env`, whereas the webapp reads `apps/web/.env`, so the webhook URL will silently not take effect; it should be derived from the script's own directory. (2) `sed -i '' -E ...` (line 68) is BSD/macOS syntax and fails on GNU sed (Linux) with "can't read : No such file or directory", so the script breaks for Linux developers.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is always formatted with hardcoded "en-US" locale
findings.body: The 'Last updated' timestamp uses `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })`. Cal.com is localized into many languages and the surrounding label is translated via `t()`, but the date/time itself will always render in US format (e.g. MM/DD/YY, 12-hour clock) regardless of the viewer's locale. Use the locale from `useLocale()` (or `dayjs` with the user's locale/timezone as elsewhere in the app) instead of the hardcoded "en-US".

findings.title: No tests for the new deleteCache mutation or the cache-status enrichment of connectedCalendars
findings.body: The PR adds a user-facing destructive mutation (`deleteCache`, including its credential-ownership check) and changes the response shape of `connectedCalendars` (new `cacheUpdatedAt` field backed by a new repository query), but adds no automated tests. At minimum, `deleteCacheHandler` should be covered for the ownership check (cannot delete another user's cache) and the happy path, and the `connectedCalendarsHandler` enrichment should be covered (including the existing-handler unit tests, which may need the `CalendarCacheRepository` mocked now that it runs an extra `groupBy`). The PR's own checklist relies entirely on manual end-to-end testing, which the notes admit was not possible locally.
